'''Ortwin Hess''' (born 1966) is a German-born theoretical [[physicist]] at [[Trinity College Dublin]] (Ireland), working in condensed matter optics. In 2016, he was awarded the [[Rumford Medal]] for his 'pioneering work in active nano-plasmonics and optical metamaterials with quantum gain'.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=2016 |title=Rumford Medal - The Royal Society |url=https://royalsociety.org/medals-and-prizes/rumford-medal/}}</ref> Bridging condensed matter theory and quantum optics he specialises in quantum [[nanophotonics]], [[plasmon]]ics, metamaterials and semiconductor laser dynamics. Since the late 1980s, he has been an author and coauthor of over 300 [[peer-review]]ed articles, the most popular of which, called {{"'}}Trapped rainbow' storage of light in metamaterials", was cited more than 400 times. He pioneered active (gain enhanced) nanoplasmonics and metamaterials with quantum gain and, in 2014, he introduced the "stopped-light lasing" principle as a novel route to cavity-free (nano-) lasing and localisation of amplified surface plasmon polaritons, giving him an [[h-index]] of 60.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?hl=en&user=0kpZGM8AAAAJ&view_op=list_works&pagesize=100|title=Ortwin Hess|publisher=[[Google Scholar]]|access-date=4 May 2014}}</ref>

==Early life==
Hess is a graduate of the [[University of Erlangen–Nuremberg]] and [[Technische Universität Berlin]]. From 1995 to 2003, he was post-doc at both the [[University of Edinburgh]] and [[Marburg University]] following by becoming faculty staff at the Institute of Technical Physics in [[Stuttgart]], Germany in 1997. In 1998, he became adjunct professor at the Department of Physics of the [[University of Stuttgart]] and then also became lecturer of Photonics at the Finnish [[Tampere University of Technology]]. From 1997 to 1998, he was visiting professor at [[Stanford University]] and in 1999/2000 visiting professor at [[LMU Munich]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.umi.surrey.ac.uk/profiles?s_id=76|title=Professor Ortwin Hess|publisher=[[University of Surrey]]|access-date=4 May 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140504071344/http://www.umi.surrey.ac.uk/profiles?s_id=76|archive-date=4 May 2014}}</ref> In July 2012, he was a visiting professor from Abbe School of Photonics. He was the Leverhulme Chair in Metamaterials at [[Imperial College London|London's Imperial College]] and co-director of the Centre for Plasmonics and Metamaterials.<ref>{{cite web|title=Ortwin Hess|publisher=Abbe School of Photonics|access-date=4 May 2014|url=http://www.asp.uni-jena.de/Visiting+Scholars/ASP+Guest+Professors/Ortwin+Hess.html|archive-date=4 May 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140504071552/http://www.asp.uni-jena.de/Visiting+Scholars/ASP+Guest+Professors/Ortwin+Hess.html}}</ref> He is currently the Professor of Quantum Nanophotonics and an SFI Research Professor in the School of Physics at Trinity College Dublin.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Ortwin Hess |url=https://ambercentre.ie/people/ortwin-hess/ |access-date=2025-07-20 |publisher=Amber Centre |language=en-US}}</ref> He also held the position of editor-in-chief of the open-access journal ''APL Quantum''.<ref name=":1" />

==Research==
Investigating slow light in metamaterials Hess has discovered and explained the 'trapped-rainbow' principle<ref>{{cite journal|author1=Tsakmakidis, K. L.|author2=Boardman, A. D.|author3=Hess, O.|year=2007|title='Trapped rainbow' storage of light in metamaterials|journal=[[Nature (journal)|Nature]]|volume=450|issue=7168|pages=397–401|doi=10.1038/nature06285|pmid=18004380|bibcode = 2007Natur.450..397T |s2cid=34711078}}</ref> by which the constituent colours of a light pulse are brought to a complete stand-still at different points inside a metamaterial (or plasmonic) heterostructure. He pioneered active metamaterials<ref>{{cite journal|author1=Hess, O.|display-authors=4|author2=Pendry, J. B.|author3=Maier, S. A.|author4=Oulton, R.|author5=Hamm, J. M.|author6=Tsakmakidis, K. L.|date=2012|title=Active nanoplasmonic metamaterials|journal=[[Nature Materials]]|volume=11|issue=7|pages=573–584|doi=10.1038/nmat3356|pmid=22717488|bibcode = 2012NatMa..11..573H }}</ref> with quantum gain,<ref>{{cite journal|author1=Hess, O.|author2=Tsakmakidis, K. L.|year=2013|title=Metamaterials with Quantum Gain|journal=[[Science (journal)|Science]]|volume=339|issue=6120|pages=654–655|doi=10.1126/science.1231254 |pmid=23393252|bibcode = 2013Sci...339..654H |s2cid=206545802}}</ref> developed the theory for optical chirality in self-organised nanoplasmonic metamaterials<ref name=am>{{cite journal|author1=Salvatore, S.|display-authors=4|author2=Demetriadou, A.|author3=Vignolini, S.|author4=Oh S. S.|author5=Wuestner, S.|author6=Yufa, N. A.|author7=Stefik, M.|author8=Wiesner, U.|author9=Baumberg, J. J.|author10=Hess. O.|author11=Steiner, U.|year=2013|title=Tunable 3D Extended Self-Assembled Gold Metamaterials with Enhanced Light Transmission|journal=[[Advanced Materials|Adv. Mater.]]|volume=25|issue=19|pages=2713–2716|doi=10.1002/adma.201300193|pmid=23553887|s2cid=40084235|doi-access=free|bibcode=2013AdM....25.2713S}}</ref><ref name=am2>{{cite journal|author1=Oh, S. S.|author2=Demetriadou, A.|author3=Wuestner, S.|author4=Hess, O.|title=On the Origin of Chirality in Nanoplasmonic Gyroid Metamaterials|journal=Adv. Mater.|volume=25|issue=4|pages=612–617|year=2012|doi=10.1002/adma.201202788|pmid=23108851|s2cid=33216292 }}</ref> and recently introduced 'stopped-light lasing'<ref name=nature>{{cite journal|title=Cavity-free plasmonic nanolasing enabled by dispersionless stoopped light|author1=Pickering, T.|display-authors=4|author2=Hamm, J. M.|author3=Page, A. F.|author4=Wuestner, S.|author5=Hess, O.|date=2014|journal=[[Nature Communications]]|volume=5|issue=4972|page=4972|doi=10.1038/ncomms5972|doi-access=free|pmid=25230337|bibcode = 2014NatCo...5.4972P |pmc=4199200}}</ref> as a novel route to cavity-free nanolasing and localisation of amplified surface plasmon polaritons (SPP) that is reminiscent of SPP-condensation.

Interest in the field of 'slow' and 'stopped' light arises from the prospect of obtaining much better control over light signals, with extremely nonlinear effects in interactions between light and matter, and optical quantum memories facilitating new architectures to process quantum information.<ref name=journals>{{cite journal|title=Completely Stopped and Dispersionless Light in Plasmonic Waveguides|author1=Tsakmakidis, K. L.|display-authors=4|author2=Pickering, T. W.|author3=Hamm, J. M.|author4=Page, A. F.|author5=Hess, O.|journal=[[Physical Review Letters]]|volume=112|article-number=167401|year=2014|issue=16 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.112.167401|pmid=24815668|bibcode=2014PhRvL.112p7401T|hdl=10044/1/19446|url=http://spiral.imperial.ac.uk/bitstream/10044/1/19446/2/PhysRevLett.112.167401.pdf|hdl-access=free|archive-date=12 August 2017|access-date=30 September 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170812181318/http://spiral.imperial.ac.uk/bitstream/10044/1/19446/2/PhysRevLett.112.167401.pdf}}</ref> With conventional dielectric materials, having a positive [[refractive index]], it is impossible to 'stop' travelling light signals completely, not least because of the presence of structural disorder.<ref name=journals/> This was an important observation, which Hess made from his extensive studies of slow light in semiconductor quantum dots<ref>{{cite journal|author1=Hess, O.|author2=Gehrig E.|title=Photonics of Quantum Dot Nanomaterials and Devices: Theory and Modelling|publisher=[[Imperial College Press]]|place=London|year=2011}}</ref><ref name=ieee>{{cite journal|author1=Gehrig, E.|display-authors=4|author2=van der Poel, M.|author3=Mork, J.|author4=Hvam, J. M.|author5=Hess, O.|year=2006|title=Dynamic spatiotemporal speed control of ultrashort pulses in quantum-dot SOAs|journal=IEEE J. Quantum Electron.|volume=42|issue=9–10|pages=1047–1054|doi=10.1109/JQE.2006.881632|bibcode=2006IJQE...42.1047G|s2cid=114706|url=http://epubs.surrey.ac.uk/50/1/fulltext.pdf}}</ref> and the dynamics of their spontaneous emission close to the stopped-light point in photonic crystals.<ref>{{cite journal|author1=Hermann, C.|author2=Hess, O.|year=2002|title=Modified spontaneous-emission rate in an inverted-opal structure with complete photonic bandgap|journal=J. Opt. Soc. Am. B|volume=19|issue=3013|page=3013|doi=10.1364/JOSAB.19.003013|bibcode=2002JOSAB..19.3013H}}</ref> Hess showed theoretically that a way to overcome this fundamental limitation of conventional media was to use nanoplasmonic waveguide structures.<ref name=nature/><ref name=journals/>

Hess has also made contributions to spatiotemporal and nonlinear dynamics in semiconductor lasers<ref name=ieee/><ref>{{cite journal|author1=Hartmann, M.|author2=Mahler, G.|author3=Hess, O.|year=2004|title=Existence of temperature on the nanoscale|journal=Phys. Rev. Lett.|volume=93|issue=80402|article-number=080402|doi=10.1103/physrevlett.93.080402|pmid=15447159|arxiv=quant-ph/0312214|bibcode=2004PhRvL..93h0402H|s2cid=8052791}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author1=Fischer, I.|author2=Hess, O.|author3=Elsasser, W.|author4=Goebel, E.|date=1994|title=High-dimensional chaotic dynamics in an external-cavity semiconductor laser|journal=Phys. Rev. Lett.|volume=73|issue=2188|doi=10.1103/physrevlett.73.2188|bibcode=1994PhRvL..73.2188F|pages=2188–2191|pmid=10056995}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author1=Gehrig, E.|author2=Hess, O.|title=Spatio-Temporal Dynamics and Quantum Fluctuations of Semiconductor Lasers|journal=Springer Tracts in Modern Physics|publisher=[[Springer Science+Business Media|Springer-Verlag]]|place=Berlin|year=2003|volume=189|doi=10.1007/b13584|bibcode=2003STMP..189.....H|isbn=978-3-540-00741-8}}</ref> and research in computational photonics. Algorithms and codes developed in his group run on high-performance parallel computers and have been used to elucidate a rich variety of aspects of modern nano-physics ranging from the definition of temperature in nanoscale systems,<ref>{{cite journal|author1=Hartmann, M.|author2=Mahler, G.|author3=Hess, O.|year=2004|title=Existence of temperature on the nanoscale|journal=Phys. Rev. Lett.|volume=93|issue=80402|article-number=080402|doi=10.1103/physrevlett.93.080402 |pmid=15447159|arxiv = quant-ph/0312214|bibcode=2004PhRvL..93h0402H|s2cid=8052791}}</ref> to optimisation of ultrashort pulses in experimentally realised quantum-dot semiconductor optical amplifiers.<ref name=ieee/> Since 2011, Hess developed the theory of optical activity in chiral nanoplasmonic metamaterials<ref name=am2/> that provided explanation of experiments on tunability in self-organised gold metamaterials.<ref name=am/>

Recently{{When|date=March 2025|reason=needs to be more specific than Recently}} Hess has started to develop "meta-lasers" and proposed "stopped-light nanolasing". This endeavor is backed by previous experience in nanoplasmonic metamaterials, quantum photonics and semiconductor lasers. Initially the goal of his work was to compensate dissipative losses in metamaterials by introducing gain.<ref>{{cite journal|author1=Wuestner, S.|display-authors=4|author2=Pusch, A.|author3=Tsakmakidis, K. L.|author4=Hamm, J. M.|author5=Hess, O.|year=2011|title=Gain and plasmon dynamics in negative-index metamaterials|journal=[[Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society A]]|volume=369|issue=1950|pages=3144–3550|doi=10.1098/rsta.2011.0140|pmid=21807726|hdl=10044/1/10160|doi-access=free|hdl-access=free|arxiv=1012.1576}}</ref> But now, one aims to create a new class of ultrafast 'stopped-light nano lasers', with unprecedented design features such as being smaller than a fifth of the wavelength and to provide a platform for integrating both light and amplified plasmons.<ref name=nature/><ref name=journals/> The latter would enable integration at the nanoscale with semiconductor chips for telecommunications.

== Honors & Awards ==
In 2016, Hess received the Rumford Medal - awarded once every year - for his 'pioneering work in active nano-plasmonics and optical metamaterials with quantum gain'.<ref name=":0" /> He is a Professor Fellow at Trinity College Dublin and a Fellow of the Institute of Physics and of Optica.<ref name=":1" /> In 2024, he was elected a Member of the [[Royal Irish Academy]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Power |first=Karen |date=2024-05-24 |title=Admittance Day 2024 |url=https://www.ria.ie/2024/05/24/admittance-day-2024/ |access-date=2025-03-05 |website=Royal Irish Academy |language=en}}</ref>
